la:noun:lar.gloss: the protective spirit of a place (particularly a household)
senses: the protective spirit of a place (particularly a household)
la:noun:lar.html:
Lār or Lars, Lartis, m.,
a prænomen of Etruscan origin (in Etruscan, usu: the prefix of the first-born, while a younger son was called Aruns. The name Lar, Lars, or Larth was an honorary appellation in Etruscan, = Engl. lord): Lars Tolumnius, rex Veientium,; ; : ad Lartem Porsenam, (nom. Lar, P.).

la:verb:largior.gloss: to grant, bestow, dispense, distribute, impart
senses: to grant, bestow, dispense, distribute, impart
la:verb:largior.html:
largĭor, ītus, 4 (ante-class. and poet.; collat. form of the
imperf. largibar, ; fut. largibere, ; inf. largirier, .—Act. collat. form, v. fin.), v. dep.
1. largus
, to give bountifully, to lavish, bestow, dispense, distribute, impart (class.; cf.: dono, suppedito).
Lit.
In gen.: amico homini mea ex crumena largiar,: ex ea (dote) largiri te illi,: cenam esurientibus,: qui eripiunt aliis, quod aliis largiantur,; cf.: ex alieno,; : agros emeritis,: largitur in servos quantum aderat pecuniae,: facile largiri de alieno,.—Of inanimate subjects: sol universis idem lucis largitur,: Gallis provinciae propinquitas multa ad copiam atque usus largitur, * .—
In partic., to give largesses, to bribe: largiundo et pollicitando magis incendere,; : exercitum largiendo corrumpere,: largiendo de alieno popularem fieri,: dictis largiri, to bestow in words, i. e. to promise without power to give: quid nunc acturu's, postquam erili filio largitu's dictis dapsilis lubentias,.—
Trop., to confer, bestow, grant, yield: Hortensio summam copiam facultatemque dicendi natura largita est,: utrisque fortuna regnum est largita,: nimium parcus in largienda civitate,: plusculum amori,: occasionem clamandi,: quidquid solamen humandi est, largior,; so, alicui occasionem impudentiae,: laetitiam alicui,: Istoscine patrem aequom morest liberis largirier?to teach, communicate,: id largiamur inertiae nostrae,give up, concede,: reipublicae injurias. to forgive, : beneficia in vulgus,: totus habenas,to give, re lax,.—Esp.: se largiri, to bestow one's society, to be free or eager in courtship: nam tu te vilem feceris, si te ultro largiere: sine ultro veniat, quaeritet, etc.,

.—

With foll. ut: si quis mihi deus largiatur, ut ex hac aetate repuerascam,would grant,.
Act. collat. form, largĭo, īre; act. imp. largi, Att. ap. ; so, Lucil. ib. —*
largītus, a, um, in pass. signif.: .

la:noun:largitio.html:
largītĭo, ōnis, f.
largior
,
a giving freely, a granting, bestowing, dispensing, distributing, imparting.
Lit.
In gen. (class.): largitio, quae fit ex re familiari, fontem ipsum benignitatis exhaurit,: largitione redemit militum voluntates,: his pauca ad spem largitionis addidit,: maximas largitiones fecit,: largitio et communicatio civitatis,a granting,: aequitatis,a distributing, dispensing,.—Prov.: largitio fundum non habet,there is no end of giving,; v. fundus.—
In partic., in a bad sense.
Bribery, corruption, esp. to obtain a public office: liberalitatem ac benignitatem ab ambitu atque largitione sejungere,: tribum turpi largitione corrumpere,: tribus largitione devinctas habere,: perniciosa,: profusissima,: nullum largitionis genus omisit,.—*
Profusion, prodigality: nullius rei, minime beneficiorum, honesta largitio est,.—
Meton., concr., largitiones, the imperial treasury, public chest, or imperial fund for presents and distributions, ; ; both sacrae (for public or state purposes) and privatae (for personal outlay),; Cod. Th. 12, 6, 13.

la:adj:largus.gloss: abundant, copious, plentiful, large, abounding in something
senses: abundant, copious, plentiful, large, abounding in something
la:adj:largus.html:
largus, a, um, adj.
perh. for lasgus; Sanscr. root lash, desire; Gr. λᾶ- in λιλαίομαι, λῆμα; cf. Lat. lascivus
,
abundant, copious, plentiful, large, much.
In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): pabula,abundant,: haustus,: semen,: imbres,; cf.: undae fluminis,: lux,; cf.: (sol) cum terras larga luce compleverit,: odores,: aër,—Comp.: largior ignis,: largiore vino usus,: largiora stipendia,: nec potentem amicum Largiora flagito,.—Sup.: munus largissimum edere,: vena largissima ferri,.—
With gen., abounding in any thing: largus lacrumarum,: opum,: fons largus aquae, : comae,: rapinae,.—
With abl.: audin' hunc, opera ut largus est nocturna?: folia larga suco,.—
In partic., giving abundantly or much, bountiful, profuse, liberal: justus, injustus: malignus, largus,: duo sunt genera largorum, quorum alteri prodigi, alteri liberales,: largissimus esse,: largus et exundans ingenii fons,: largus animo,of a generous disposition,: promissis,liberal in promises,: natura,.—Comp.: Quid ego concesso pedibus, linguā largior?. —Poet.: largus animae,prodigal of life,.—With inf.: spes donare novas largus,.—Hence, adv. in three forms.
largē (class.), abundantly, plentifully, bountifully, liberally: large blandus,: large dare,: large effuseque donare,: large et copiose aliquid comparare,: munifice et large dari,: large atque honorifice promittere,: large liberaliterque aestimare,: ministrare libertatem alicui,: senatus consultum large factum,: large florescens,: large frequentantibus (locum),in great numbers,: large amplecti,widely,; .—Comp.: dare largius,: ne potum largius aequo Rideat,.—Sup.: copia quam largissime facta, Zumpt N. cr. (Klotz, largissima), .—
largĭter, largely, in abundance, plentifully, much; greatly, far (rare in class. prose; not used by Cic.),: peccavisti largiter,; cf. : apud finitimas civitates largiter posse, to have great weight or influence, : distare,: auferre,; : discrepare,: largius a prisca consuetudine movere,.—
Substantively, with gen. (anteand post-class.): credo, illic inesse auri et argenti largiter,; cf.: largiter mercedis indipiscar,. —*
largĭtus, copiously: quid lacrimas largitus? Afran. ap. (Com. Fragm. v. 212 Rib.).

la:noun:largitas.html:
largĭtas, ātis, f.
1. largus
,
abundance, bounty, liberality (rare but class.): largitas nimia, opp. parsimonia,: quae istaec subita est largitas?: tui muneris,: terra fruges cum maxima largitate fundit,.

la:noun:largitor.html:
largītor, ōris, m.
largior
,
a liberal giver, a bestower, granter, dispenser, distributer, imparter.
In gen. (rare; not in Cic.): multarum rerum ac maxume pecuniae largitor,: largitor voluntarius repente senatus factus,: minime largitore duce,liberal,; cf. praedae,: Bacche, sacri largitor laticis,dispenser,.—
In partic., in a bad sense, a briber (class.): exsistunt in re publica plerumque largitores et factiosi,: cujuscumque tribus largitor esset,: Lentulum largitorem et prodigum non putat,a spendthrift, squanderer,.

la:other:Lares.gloss: a city in Africa situated on the valley of the Bagrada, now Lorbeus
senses: a city in Africa situated on the valley of the Bagrada, now Lorbeus
la:other:Lares.html:
Lăres (old form † Lăses, Inscr. Fratr. Arval.; cf. Müll.), um and ĭum (Larum, Müll.; ; ; ; :
Larium,), m.
old Lat. Lases; Etrusc. Laran, Lalan; root las-; cf. lascivus
, tutelar deities, Lares, belonging orig. to the Etruscan religion, and worshipped especially as the presiders over and protectors of a particular locality (cf. Otfr. Müll. Etrusc. 2, p. 90 sq.): praestites,the tutelar deities of an entire city,: mille Lares geniumque ducis, qui tradidit illos, urbs habet,: Puteolanae civitatis,: civitatum, Inscr. ap. Grut. p. 10, 2: vicorum,: rurales, Inscr. ap. Grut. p. 251: compitales,of cross - roads,; called also Lares compitalicii, Philarg. ad : viales,worshipped by the road-side,: permarini,tutelar deities of the sea,: caelipotentes, Inscr. ap. .—Sing.: Lari viali,; : eundem esse Genium et Larem, multi veteres memoriae prodiderunt,.—
Most commonly the Lares (as familiares or domestici), the tutelar deities of a house, household gods, domestic Lares (whose images stood on the hearth in a little shrine, aedes, or in a small chapel, lararium); as the tutelar deities of each particular dwelling, also in sing.: Lar, Laris, m.
In plur.: rem divinam facere Laribus familiaribus,: sanctis Penatium deorum Larumque familiarium sedibus,; : ad aedem Larum,: immolet aequis porcum Laribus,: Laribus tuum Miscet numen,. —
In sing.: ego Lar sum familiaris, ex hac familia,: haec imponuntur in foco nostro dari,: familiae Lar pater, alium Larem persequi,—
Meton., a hearth, dwelling, home (class.; usually in sing.): larem corona nostrum decorari volo,: relinquent larem familiarem suum?: ad suum larem familiarem redire,, § 125: nobis larem familiarem nusquam ullum esse?: paternus,: patrius,; cf.: avitus apto Cum lare fundus,: gaudens lare certo,: parvo sub lare,: conductus,: deserere larem,to abandon one's home,: pelli lare,to be driven from a place,: alumnus laris Antenorei,i. e. of the city of Padua,: ob eam rem tibi Lare commercioque interdico, Vet. Formul. ap. .—
In plur., : jussa pars mutare lares,.—Poet., of a bird's nest: avis in ramo tecta laremque parat,: cum rapit Halcyones miserae fetumque laremque,.

banquet ghost: a skeleton doll with movable joints seated at the banquet table at Roman parties in a fashion that came about in the 1st century AD
la:noun:larva.html:
larva (ante-class. as trisyl. lārŭa), ae, f.
2. lar
,
a ghost, spectre: larvae stimulant virum,: amator qui me et uxorem ludificatust larva,; : cum mortuis non nisi larvas luctari, Plin. praef. H. N. § 31.—As a term of reproach, hobgoblin, scarecrow: etiam loquere larŭa?: nam haec quidem edepol larvarum plenast,possessed,.—
Transf.
A mask (cf. persona): nil illi larva et tragicis opus esse cothurnis,.—
A skeleton, .

la:verb:larvo.html:
larvo, no
perf., ātum (part. ante-class. larŭātus), 1, v. a.
larva
, to bewitch, enchant (ante- and post-class., and used almost exclusively in the part. perf.): artus larvari, Firm. Math. 3, 14.—P. a. as subst.: larvans, ntis, m., an enchanter, a dealer in magic: hunc denique qui larvam putat ipse est larvans, Hildeb. (al. larvatus).—Part. perf.: larŭātus, a, um, bewitched, enchanted: quid illi esse morbi dixeras? ... Num larvatust aut cerritus?: pro laruato te circumferam, id. Fragm. ap. .
